How low the sound falls between the steps. 0 dB means no cut, then down to -60 dB; the top position is fully silent.
Edge softness of every step. Low is a hard chop, high is a soft pulse.
Curve of each open step. 0 keeps it flat. Higher values let the note fall away toward the cut level before the next step, like a pluck.
Lets the gap before an open step rise back up toward full level, a reverse swell into the next note. 0 is off.
Final level trim after the limiter, -12 to +12 dB.
Stage 1, opamp drive: smooth tanh saturation.
Stage 2, transistor: asymmetric, adds even harmonics for warmth and weight.
Stage 3, fuzz: lopsided and gritty with a smooth octave up growl.
Blend between the clean and the driven sound.
High pass that clears the low mids so the kick and bass keep their pocket. Pads and leads about 250 to 300 Hz, bass off.
Everything below this frequency is made mono (about 120 Hz). Keeps the low end solid on any system. The preview does not do this, the plugin will.
Boost or cut around 3 kHz in the centre so the lead cuts through.
High pass on the sides only, so the width stays out of the low end.
High shelf at 10 kHz for sparkle.
More or less punch at the start of each note.
More or less of the body after the start.
How much of the harsh peaks is pulled down. It only acts when they stick out.
Level where the compressor starts. Set for about 1.5 to 2 dB of gain reduction.
Slow attack keeps the punch. About 30 ms.
Blend of a heavily squashed copy (parallel compression) for size and density.
How wide the sound gets.
Speed of the slow pan.
How far the sound moves left and right.
Trance gate on or off. It chops the sound into steps in time with the tempo.
Master switch of the whole processing chain. On by default, so every sound comes out ready for a track. Switch it off to hear the raw synth.
Reset every module to the settings made for the chosen sound type.
Drive stack on or off. Three stages in a row: opamp drive, transistor, fuzz (from PurrOne).

Peak reduction, 0 to 100 like the hardware scale. More means more levelling. 22 gives about 2 to 3 dB on big chords.
Make up gain after the leveller, 0 to 100 like the hardware scale. 50 adds no extra gain.
Blend of the levelled and the dry sound.
Blend of the squeezed and the dry sound, like the depth of an OTT. 12 to 18 percent is plenty on a synth that is already bright.

Limiter lookahead in half milliseconds. More is cleaner but adds latency.
Blend of the squeezed and the dry sound. Below 100 percent is parallel compression.
